Well, honestly, I think I'm pretty much always talking. It doesn't really matter if I'm alone or with people, the engine's just always running, you know? But it definitely causes more problems when I'm around others. Like at school... I'll go into a parent conference or a staff meeting, and I'll tell myself, "Okay, just keep it brief this time. Just stick to the bullet points." And then before I know it, I hear myself giving three different examples of a student's behavior, plus a story about something that happened in my classroom last Tuesday, and then I'm throwing out all these ideas for new curriculum plans that literally nobody asked for.

The principal, Mr. Harrison, he does this thing where he taps his pen on his clipboard when he wants you to leave. He always uses those blue Pilot G2 pens. The 0.7 millimeter ones. I prefer the 0.5 myself, the finer point just looks neater when you're grading papers. I grade entirely in green ink now. Red is too aggressive, they say. I read this whole article about color psychology in education. It said green is calming, like nature. Which makes sense, because I love being out in the woods. When I was a kid, we lived right next to this massive state park, and my brother and I would just disappear into the trees for hours. We built this incredible treehouse out of scrap wood we found behind a construction site. We even rigged up a pulley system with a bucket to haul up our snacks. My mom used to pack us these bologna sandwiches on white bread with the crusts cut off...
